title: Ask the Guru before the question scatters
summary: The shabad lets confusion speak plainly, then sends it to the True Guru instead of the crowd. The turn is not another option to sample, but accepting hukam and letting selfishness be pulled from the root.
takeaway: Bring the question to the Guru before the crowd multiplies it.
lifeApplication: When uncertainty starts collecting voices, pause before the next search. Put the real question before the Guru and let one line of hukam answer before anyone else does.

source.shortMeaning: The seeking heart is steadied by asking the Guru and accepting hukam instead of multiplying voices.
source.lifeApplication: When uncertainty spreads, ask the Guru before you ask the crowd.

evidence.coreClaim: The seeking heart is steadied by taking its question to the Guru and accepting hukam.
evidence.turn: Clarity begins when the question stops scattering and bows before the True Guru.
evidence.practicalImplication: When uncertainty starts collecting voices, pause before the next search. Put the real question before the Guru and let one line of hukam answer before anyone else does.
